listing.name: Faction Doctrine Controller
listing.summary: Adds a Lunaconfig menu that allows you to change select doctrine values of all factions.
listing.aiSummary: Adds a configuration menu to adjust faction doctrine values like fleet size and ship class.

description:
Adds a Lunaconfig menu that allows you to change select doctrine values of all factions.

Change all factions' shipSize (average ship class) and numShips (fleet size) values.
Exclude specific factions from these changes with a csv blacklist.

Set a limit on how large total fleet size multipliers can be.
Options for heavy industries (and related industries) to increase a faction's global fleet sizes.
Increase or decrease the frequency for ships of user defined tags in the player's fleets (e.g. midline_package, pirate_package, etc.)
Decrease the frequency of modded ships in the vanilla factions' fleets (configurable).
Normalize various Nexerelin faction relationship settings.

Safe to add or remove to and from saves-in-progress.

Pictures

Requires LunaLib.

Download

  • Normalize various Nexerelin faction relationship settings.

Safe to add or remove to and from saves-in-progress.

changelog.1.1.6:
- Fixed a "bug" where the features to apply tag frequencies to the player faction and modify modded ship frequencies were non-functional.
 - They were technically working but didn't actually apply the intended effect in any meaningful way.
changelog.1.1.5:
- Added a new feature to change the frequency of modded ships for specific factions.
 - data\config\FDC_ModTagFrequencyFactions.csv is where you define which factions receive this change, and what the multiplier will be on a faction-by-faction basis.
 - data\config\FDC_Mod_Whitelist.csv allows you to exclude certain mods from this toggle – meaning their ships will not have their frequencies modified at all.
changelog.1.1.4:
- Deprecated "Remove Trash Ships" option.
- The tag frequency settings now resets the frequencies periodically and on game save, i.e. you can effectively disable the option mid-game now rather than having the frequencies 'stick' permanently.
